subject: Service resilience discovery — Aurora Financial (post-call summary & next steps)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@aurorafin.com>, infra@aurorafin.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Service resilience discovery — Aurora Financial (post-call summary & next steps)

Hi Ravi / infra team,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I’ve attached a short PDF with the notes (aurora_postcall_notes.pdf).

High-level pain points we heard
- Production outages during peak batch runs (Nov and Sep incidents) causing degraded inference and customer-facing timeouts.
- Lack of predictable tail latency under burst load; current autoscaling takes too long to stabilize.
- Limited fallbacks: single-region deployment and no lower-cost model tier for graceful degradation.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Inference served on a k8s cluster in us-west-2 running single-tenant model endpoints behind an API gateway.
- Primary model: open-llm-large (fp16), served on A100-equivalent.
- Observability: basic Prometheus + ELK, limited synthetic traffic for SLO verification.

Success criteria you named
- Reduce customer-facing errors during load spikes to <0.1% per month (SLI).
- P95 latency target <= 200ms for common paths; p99 as a secondary objective.
- Automatic graceful degradation with a cost-conscious fallback within 30s of overload.
- Clear playbook and runbook for incidents (RTO goal: <5 minutes to failover/graceful degrade).

Incident history you shared (summary)
- 2026-11-16: Backfill batch coincided with scheduled deploy -> 18min outage, 11% request errors.
- 2026-09-04: Region-wide cloud maintenance caused elevated latencies for ~45min.
(please confirm if these dates/impacts need correction)

Preliminary ideas we discussed
- Multi-region routing with regional fallbacks and automated model variant failover (full model -> quantized smaller model).
- Short-circuiting and caching for repeat prefixes to reduce token compute during bursts.
- Dedicated reserved capacity for critical endpoints plus a low-cost shared pool for bursty traffic.
- SLO-focused synthetic tests in the console to verify changes before rollout.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Tech workshop (60–90m) to validate workload profile and run a small synthetic test: Karthik to lead (propose Wed/Thu next week).
2) I'll send a short SLA draft and a mutual action plan (MAP) we can iterate on.
3) We’ll provide an example graceful-degradation runbook + a sample config for multi-region routing.
4) Share SOC2 summary and required security questionnaire items before any PoC/contract work.

Attachments included: aurora_postcall_notes.pdf (summary), runbook_snapshot.txt (sample runbook excerpt).

If anything above is misremembered, reply with corrections and I’ll update the doc. Otherwise I’ll loop Karthik in to schedule the workshop and Marissa will start a MAP in HubSpot.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Service resilience discovery — Aurora Financial (post-call summary & next steps)

Diego — thanks for the thorough summary. This matches our notes closely. A few clarifications and extra context from the infra side: 

Incident clarifications
- 2026-11-16 incident: root cause was a combination of a large backfill job saturating GPU memory and a staggered deploy that increased cold-start tokenization latency. Impact: roughly 18 minutes with elevated error rate; ~1.8k failed inference requests.
- 2026-09-04: correct — cloud provider maintenance caused a regional networking flap; services degraded for ~45 minutes but recovered without operator intervention.

Priority items for us
- Short-term: a configuration that gives us a safe fallback (lower-capacity model + per-customer rate limits) to keep latency stable while we debug autoscaling.
- Mid-term: dedicated capacity for top-3 SLAs customers starting Q1; need predictable throughput pricing to evaluate budget.
- Compliance: need to see SOC2 plus data retention options (we have regulatory requirements in EU workloads even for US customers).

Timing
- We’re targeting an internal decision for PoC by mid-December. A tech workshop next week is great — Wed after 10am PT looks good for our infra leads.

One ask: can your team sketch a simple two-tier fallback approach (primary model + micro-quantized fallback) with expected token-cost delta and latency estimates so we can present to procurement?

Appreciate it — I’ll confirm attendees for Wed.

— Ravi
Ravi Menon
Head of Platform Engineering | Aurora Financial
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@aurorafin.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service resilience discovery — Aurora Financial (post-call summary & next steps)

Thanks Ravi — quick technical sketch ahead of the workshop, so everyone has something concrete to react to.

Two-tier fallback proposal (sketch):
- Primary: open-llm-large, fp16, running on dedicated A100-equivalent instances for critical endpoints.
- Fallback: open-llm-medium quantized (4-bit) — expected characteristics: ~40–60% reduction in per-token compute, P95 latency increase +30–60ms vs primary in same hw, but much higher throughput per GPU.
- Routing: request routed to primary regional pool. If queue depth or token-per-second exceeds threshold for >10s, traffic overflow to fallback pool in same region. If whole region unhealthy, auto-switch to secondary region with weighted failover rules.

Expected economics (very rough)
- Fallback reduces per-token cost by ~50% for inference compute.
- With caching and prefix reuse we often see 15–25% token savings on re-issued queries.

SLO suggestions (to discuss at workshop)
- P95 latency target: <= 200ms for 90% of routes; P99 elastic target tracked as a hardship metric.
- Error budget objective: keep monthly request failures <0.1% for critical routes.
- Graceful degradation window: automatic fallback engagement within 30s of sustained overload; manual SLA failover for region-level incidents.

Plan for workshop
- Live synthetic traffic run with your representative payloads to surface bottlenecks.
- Walk through our console’s SLO and synthetic configuration.
- Validate fallback timing and observe token-cost delta in a short run (15–30m).

Attachments: I’ve added a proposed SLA draft we can iterate on (proposed_sla_draft.docx) and a short runbook snippet (runbook_snapshot.txt).

I’ll be on the Wed slot after 10am PT. Diego — please share the final invite and attendee list.

— Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

I’ll upload the post-call notes and the draft SLA to the Drive folder and send the calendar invite with the Workshop agenda.
